segments.t: Upstairs in the hotel corridor, the strict commission chairwoman measures the hallway and inspects a guest room, criticizing the lighting and wrinkled bedding. Mikhail cheerfully brushes off every flaw as a trifle and leads them to a suite that turns out to be occupied.
Что-то не так?
Коридор у вас должен быть на пять сантиметров шире.
Всё исправлено!
Постель помята.
Уборка номеров — три балла.
Это такие пустяки!
У нас всё отлично, на пять звёзд.
Мы не знали, что этот люкс занят.
Пройдёмте в другой.
А вы что, не в курсе?
Какие номера у вас свободны, какие заняты?
Сейчас всё проверим!
Now let's go back through their conversation line by line and unpack the Russian phrasing.
Что-то не так?
'Is something wrong?' The meaning hinges on 'something' working together with 'so' in spoken Russian.
Коридор у вас должен быть на пять сантиметров шире.
'Your corridor must be five centimeters wider.' the inspector chooses the respectful plural 'you' alongside 'wider' to keep a polite distance. Mikhail answers right away.
Всё исправлено!
'Everything is fixed!' Mikhail brings out the contrast between 'everything' and 'fixed' in a few short words.
Постель помята.
'The bed is rumpled.' the inspector brings out the contrast between 'bedding' and 'rumpled' in a few short words.
Уборка номеров — три балла.
'Room housekeeping is three points.' the inspector anchors the line on 'cleaning', while 'points' completes the thought. Mikhail answers right away.
Это такие пустяки!
'Those are such trifles!' The grammar packs 'this' and 'trifles' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
У нас всё отлично, на пять звёзд.
'Everything with us is excellent, worthy of five stars.' The grammar packs 'at' and 'stars' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
Мы не знали, что этот люкс занят.
'We did not know that this suite was occupied.' The plural past ending '-li' on the verb for 'to know' covers a group or the polite 'you'.
Пройдёмте в другой.
'Let us proceed to another one.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'let's go' and finishing on 'another'.
А вы что, не в курсе?
'Are you not aware?' the inspector chooses the respectful plural 'you' alongside 'course' to keep a polite distance.
Какие номера у вас свободны, какие заняты?
'Which rooms of yours are vacant and which are occupied?' In Russian, the idea of 'what' flows naturally into 'occupied' without extra filler words. Mikhail answers right away.
Сейчас всё проверим!

'We will check everything right now!' Mikhail brings out the contrast between 'now' and 'everything' in a few short words. Alright, let's hear the entire conversation one more time from start to finish.

And that finishes the corridor inspection scene. Notice the short passive participles for fixed, rumpled, vacant, and occupied as the inspector grades the hotel. See you in the next scene.
